what_its_for: Leflunomide is used to treat rheumatoid arthritis in adults. It helps reduce joint pain, swelling, and stiffness by calming down your immune system, which is attacking your own joints.
how_to_take: Take leflunomide by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush or chew the tablet.
dosing: Your doctor will usually start you on a higher loading dose (100 mg once a day for 3 days) to get the medicine working faster, then switch you to the regular maintenance dose (10 mg or 20 mg once a day). Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different based on your needs.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store leflunomide at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store in a dry place, such as a cabinet — not in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can increase the risk of liver damage. Do not get live vaccines (such as the live flu vaccine) while taking this medicine. Avoid becoming pregnant — leflunomide can cause serious birth defects. Both men and women must use reliable birth control during treatment and for a period of time after stopping the medication. Talk to your doctor before trying to conceive, as a special washout procedure may be needed. Avoid contact with people who are sick, as this medicine can weaken your immune system.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain (possible liver problems); unusual bruising or bleeding; signs of infection such as fever, chills, sore throat, or cough that won't go away; numbness or tingling in your hands or feet; severe skin rash, blistering, or peeling; shortness of breath or new or worsening cough; or if you think you might be pregnant. Also tell your doctor if you have high blood pressure, as this medicine can raise blood pressure.
when_it_works: Leflunomide is a slow-acting medicine. You may start to notice some improvement in your joint pain and swelling within 4 to 6 weeks, but it can take up to 3 to 6 months to feel the full benefit. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you don't feel better right away.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do NOT use leflunomide if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause serious harm or birth defects to an unborn baby. It must also not be used while breastfeeding. Men who want to father a child should speak with their doctor, as a washout procedure may be needed. Liver disease: This medicine is not recommended for people with significant liver problems. Your doctor will check your liver with blood tests regularly. Elderly patients: Older adults may need closer monitoring for side effects. Children: Leflunomide is not approved for use in children.
